The parkour, and being able to get into windows on random floors — these are the only decent things in this game. And they are crippled by the fighting system which degraded so much that I simply avoid fighting zombies instead of slashing through them wherever I go.

Like, it is supposed to be a zombie-slasher game, but for some reason the zombies so rarely get sliced, that most of the time you just bluntly beat them half to death before executing a finisher move that has just a couple of predefined animations.

That was not the problem with Dying Light 1 — there I could aimlessly roam around the world, slashing zombies for my own amusement. In Dying Light 2 though, even just mindlessly parkouring is no fun, since there's nothing fun to explore.

Therefore, my playthrough quickly deteriorated into running through the story or side quests. The problem is, neither is good. There are some decent side quests I found interesting and engaging, but even they are usually half-assed. Like that time I fetched a toy stolen from a little girl, only to NOT EVEN RETURN IT to the girl. Or like when each time I decide to snitch on a culprit, the plot conveniently makes me kill them instead. But to be fair, the plot with the lost kids and dog was a particularly well written one, and overall implemented fine.

The main plot, as far as I played, could be enjoyable enough if not for the weakest illusion of choice I've seen in a game with the most absurdly written dialogs that I've simply started skipping — they didn't say much anyway, but sure used a lot of words. And that's a shame, because the characters seem interesting and memorable, and the factions have a very good composition. 

As for the world where the story takes place, it is so far off from the original Dying Light world, that I simply don't like it — it fails expectations set by the first game. Stylistically, that is. In general, it works well enough for the gameplay — the parkour is good enough, and the idea of having a lot of open windows to get into is very nice.

What I don't like about the gameplay, is just how obviously they copied Far Cry in the various base-capturing mechanic. In the first Dying Light they had it done so well and subtle, but this game just screams "You're playing a Far Cry" as it's war cry. And it's not even "a zombie Far Cry", it is just "a Far Cry" — i didn't even notice having to fight zombies to capture a safe zone anymore. And for human bases you obviously only get to fight people.

Which reminds me, that most of the main plot's fighting interactions so far were either the largely optional stealth kills of sleeping zombies, or the mandatory commiting war crimes against humanity. Which are not exactly things I'd expect to do in a zombie slasher.

Also, the paraglider is not really fun, mostly just a thing you have to use. So yeah, I'm deleting this game before even getting to the grappling hook.

tldr:  Dying Light 1 was an action horror game featuring parkour with stealth elements and opportunities.
Dying Light 2 is a stealth horror game with action elements and parkour opportunities.  

There's nothing in Dying Light 2 that can't be found being done better in zombie games like the first Dying Light, Dead Island, or Dead Island Riptide.  If you're a fan of those games, and are hoping Dying Light 2 is going to keep the high energy parkour action going---well, it's just not.  Dying Light 2 is a ponderous slog compared to its predecessor.  Watch the first Steam trailer and notice how all the player POV is during DAYLIGHT . . . because nighttime is all about creeping and stealth and is boring to watch in a video.

In DL1 the most terrifying and dangerous zombies haunted the darkness, so not being out at night was a primary device creating tension in the game.  At night the zombies were faster and deadlier and stealth becomes a key consideration to player survival.  With the exception of a couple missions, it was entirely up to the player how much of this "night game" they wanted to play, allowing for players to shape the tone and expand the action of the game for themselves. 

From the outset Dying Light 2 seems determined that you WILL spend a lot of time in slowly, carefully, tediously creeping around in the dark.  In DL2 the "day game" "night game" choice has been functionally removed from the player.  G'bye parkour-filled, action-packed "day game" fun we experienced DL1.  

I'm just not interested in being forced to do a lot of stealth in a game I bought for its parkour mechanics and zombie slaying violence.

I'll never get my money's worth out of playing Dying Light 2 because it's not a game I would've ever spent any money on if I'd known it was going to be such a bore.

Dying light 2 is not at all what I expected it to be. The game is decent at best and its a very biased opinion to rate this game as "decent". 

The parkour is about the only good aspect of this game, though it loses its realism in grounded parkour. They introduced a new kind of grappling hook which was pretty cool. The horror aspect of the nighttime in this game is garbage, I was able to kill a volatile very quickly in to the game. I was level 4 farming volatiles, safe to say that if you want to play a zombie horror game this is not the game for you. The CO OP is super buggy, constantly glitching me and my friends out of the elevator, despawning enemies forcing us to log back in to the game.

 The game is heavily server sided and it auto teleports you evertime your teammate gets close to the mission point. I heavily dislike how arcadey and parkour game with zombies this game is. You have to go out of your way and go to a badly engineered safe zone for the simplest thing like repairing your weapon. Aiden is a pussy, he gets punched in the face every other time and he can not tell a traitor from a billion miles away. The dialogue in this game is extremely stretched and the npcs are talking about nonsense majority of the cutscenes.

The paraglider makes it extremely easy to avoid any kind of danger and it fully removes the terrifying aspect of running away like the 2 other games. Dont even get me started  on Hakon and Lawan.. I am 99 percent sure Hakon is gay with all the time he caresses aiden and constantly wants to talk to this guy. I swear the dialogue with hakon adds  up to 2 hours of the game. And most of the missions were genuine slop, "get lawan's shoes"... what does getting lawans shoes add to the story? other than finding out that hakon is not truly gay and has been with a woman and isnt the incel he appears to be nothing else is added to the game. Most of the quests are turning on stuff and going places getting absolutely nothing done.

The game started off strong, introducing inhibitors and the bracelets really added on to the post apocalyptic  vibe that people are settling in and getting used to life in the apocalypse. Other than that the story is rushed and the premise that you are looking for someone you havent seen since you were kids and knowing that she isnt even your biological sister is trash as fuck. The story is extremely rushed and to cover it up, techland drags it with 3 minute dialogues. I also do not understand how techland decides to make us listen to a jackass dying and talking to us like we have been friends with them for a while. majority of the times we have never even met the characters that have a 4 minute speech while they are bleeding out.

Bloody ties is the worst dlc the game couldve introduced. I also do not understand how a game that you as a developer know isnt as strong in terms of story like the other games gives you the brilliant idea to give the character stamina while climbing. Majority of the parkour other than the basics is just button smashing and hoping to do a move you have yet to see. The skill tree is no where near as exciting to grind for and neither is it hard or challenging to upgrade but the combat skill tree sucks balls. It is also just forcing you to keep playing by not making you fully level up your skill tree and making you redo the entire story again just for you to get 3 more skills in the skill tree.

The bossfight is a massive letdown. The boss is a super easy fight and hyper repetitive. as soon as waltz hits the last phase all he does is just run away. When you get to the final cutscene a disabled chick does more convincing than aiden and you just stand there like a cuck until the key is thrown into the lava. At least with the ending I got. Everytime you think you are going to win a boss segment, you get knocked out and lose the dopamine of beating  the low lifes that tried fighting you. The renegades straight up sound goofy and are  not intimidating at all, they sound like frogs.

Overall this game has its pros but is full of cons, if you expected that this game would be peak because of the 5 years of support it has been getting, no it is not and it looks like a mobile game with all the ads in the loading screen. If you want to parkour and live though this post apocalyptic world, this game is for you, but dont expect it to be a fun grind. Although, if you are looking for a scary game with a compelling story this game isnt for you.

Dying Light 1 feels incredible to play, both its main game and DLC. Story isn't great but it feeds the gameplay well. It's also the first time during the console generation switch (360 to xbone) where I felt the game truly took advantage of its new hardware, looking incredible and feeling dynamic in both visuals and gameplay.

So, snagging DL2 on the steam sale I felt it was time to finally try things out. Not only does the game feel like a mobile game, it plays worse, too. Sure, I've only played about an hour of the game, but immediately the combat feels off. Not only do the weapons have virtually no impact, there's the introduction of these quick-kills by pressing F that are sometimes short, sometimes long, and ultimately remove me from combat.

Also, admittedly, the aesthetic of the game is very strange. It feels very coorporate, whereas the first game felt focused. It opens explaining the world had a cure, preventing the spread of the disease, but then a new strain wiped out the planet (so... why tell me there was a cure?) so everything's post-apocalyptic. But, also, our characters all dress in medieval wear. It all feels very LARP-coded (as in actual Live-Action Role-Play). It's not an aesthetic I would have considered "Dying Light" coded by any means. 

I only knew the game had a bad launch, but learning the game has been greatly altered since it released feels strange. The prologue is skippable, but I decided to try it because it's basically the tutorial of the game, but then read it has been changed multiple times. I guess I'm not that bothered by it, but it's a weird choice that kinda speaks to many other choices I've near-immediately noticed seem... off. I imagine this game went through multiple iterations, director changes, and all-in-all feels like its held together by tape and twist-ties.

Idk. I'm gonna try it out for another 50-minutes, but I don't want to cross the 2-hour mark because I'm seriously considering refunding my purchase. I'll jump into The Beast since I hear that's a better game overall. It also looks more aesthetically like the original game. Cause this feels like an absolute mess. If I return it, maybe I'll rebuy it when it's VERY cheap. But after playing through the first game a second time, then playing through The Following and really enjoying a lot of that, this immediately feels like several steps backward.

I want to be clear that this is a downgrade compared to the first game but that does not make it a bad game.

I already knew going into this that what was promised at E3 wasnt going to happen and the choices were not as impactful as I'd hoped.
I never felt like I made an impact or change by doing any story, side quests, windmills, etc 
The mission things were a complete waste of time and very disappointed that I couldn't get any more than a pistol because they're locked behind essentially what is the chore list.
Certain parts felt extremely repetitive like the electrical stations and metros.

The variety and type of missions in Dying Light 2 is reminiscent of DL but better. One bug is that it rains indoors. This game also requires a better than average rig to get the best performance out of it and my 9700k struggles.

So I completed Dying Light 2 on the XBOX X when it was first released and still own it on disc. It was fun, and enjoyable considering the type of games I enjoy. Post-Apocalypse games, literature and media have always interested me. Especially zombies which is a given considering what most of us grew up watching and playing games about.

Harran of the original game was exciting, trying to survive by travelling by and at night avoiding the Volatiles. Villedor of DY2 is just as expansive, taking place in an Eastern European city that walled itself off to first contain the virus only for those very same walls to save it's inhabitants when the virus affected the entire world.

I quite enjoyed the Faction system; with the Peacekeepers and the Survivors, deciding who to help and assist with the Renegades as the enemy faction. Discovering outposts and deciding who would get it, with different benefits to whichever faction you side with.

The combat of melee being primarily your way of fighting the infected and the Renegades and other human threats makes a return, with guns coming in later in the game. 

Similar games have come a long way from say Dead Island, expanding in lore but also gameplay mechanics. For fans of the original Dying Light, the sequel is as enjoyable. For those who haven't played it, think Dead Island expanded upon in many different ways.

I remember paying half-price for DL2 on XBOX, and I didn't regret. This being Steam there are I would say daily events and discounts, or bundles of the Dying Light franchise so it's worth buying when one is on. Get lost in a world where humanity is in a corner, against all odds trying to scratch out a life and fighting the infected and humans who wants to rule the world. A simple concept. 

8/10

[h1][b] TLDR: While the parkour remains excellent, nearly everything else feels like a step back from Dying Light 1. [/b] [/h1]

[h1]PROS: [/h1]
➕Parkour is great
➕Story-driven choices that impact the narrative outcome

[h1]CONS: [/h1]
➖Enemy AI seems buggy and occasionally just “Shuts off”
➖Excessive pointless zombie spawns - literally 3 melee attacks suddenly spawns multiple fast infected
➖Sorting in inventory never saves
➖Narrative isn’t that interesting
➖Most quests are boring fetch quests
➖Obnoxious and constant audio cues that you cannot disable (constantly notifies of ANY nearby event)
➖Combat skill tree is boring

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Synikx/recommended/239140?snr=1_5_9__402]My review for Dying Light (DL1) is here[/url]

[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
The game world takes place in a city called Villedor in 2036, 22 years after the events of DL1. The setting is mostly similar to Harran, the city from DL1. There are two main areas, a smaller village-like starting area that is a bit more rural, and the city proper, with larger buildings and a downtown-like area. 
Regardless of the differences, every building interior looks like every other and no matter how sheltered or locked down a place has been for decades, there’s always somehow zombies waiting for you inside. The exploration is good, and there are tons of random things to do in the open world. Think like an Ubisoft game, and all the good, and bad, that comes with it. 


The narrative to me was a big let down. You play as Aiden who is a “Pilgrim”. Basically what Dying Light has branded to be some sort of long-distance parkour enthusiast deliverymen. Aiden has come to Villedor to find his sister and thus begins the search. 
The story is just all over the place. I really like how there are (seemingly) big decision points to make, but these don’t seem to have a big effect on the story other than some slightly different cutscenes, dialogue, and the ending cutscene. I got about 20 hours into it before I was starting to get bored of the disappointing fetch quest side missions, and the main story itself. While there are some revelations near the end, the story never hit a positive note after dragging on. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
The general gameplay loop is typical of an open world game - completing mission objectives from one area to another. 
Coming from DL1, there are some big changes, and most of them are not positive. 
The parkour remains the best part of the game, by far., and I think it’s improved a bit. Jumping from the top of towers still gives that white-knuckle tense feeling, so it’s still great there. Adding to the already good traversal mechanics are the paraglider and a grappling hook. Though DL1 had a grappling hook, it’s not bound to a talent, you get it about 60% of the way through the story. 
The night elements have also changed. Now, you have a timer that forces you to either use a consumable or reach a UV light before it runs out, else its game over.
The RPG-like gear system has been expanded from just weapons to include gear. I didn’t find this very meaningful and the game could have done without it. 
Speaking of talents, there are two trees - combat and parkour. The combat tree I found terribly boring, but the parkour tree was good. 

The difficulty is more on the easier side. The few times I died were all because of failed parkour attempts and not the combat. Though with the combat, the Volatiles will still mess you up. The regular zombies are just a hindrance, and often annoying as the runners constantly show up when doing basic attacks against any enemy

[h1] [b] Technical (Graphics/Performance) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
I found the graphics to be this weird middle area between PS4 and PS4-era fidelity. The environments and world look great, if repetitive, but the character design and animations are a step lower. 
I played fully maxed and felt the performance was good. 
Of note is the constant bugs. I hear this has been improved with post-launch patches, but I still ran into things constantly. The most egregious is the enemy AI. The AI would occasionally literally “Turn off” and the enemies would just stand there. Also the Volatile chase sequences were a bit of a joke with how poor the AI is at following you 

1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSD  

[h1] [b] Audio – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
The music wasn’t great. In fact, I ended up turning it down because it was getting annoying. 
There’s also a sound effect, like sort of deep “Ding” that plays when an event near you is active, which happens [b]all the time[/b]. I couldn’t find a way to turn it off, but it really takes you out of the game with the constant sound. 
The voice acting is good. 

[h1] [b] Replay Factor (Longevity) – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
There is NG+ and achievements. Perhaps the big draw would be co-op and the choices available within the campaign, even if they are a bit lackluster. Still, I think there’s some good replay value here. 

[h1] [b] Final Verdict – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
Dying Light 2 (DL2) simply isn’t a great game. It lacks something that made DL1 so special. If I had to attribute this downfall to features specifically, it would be the narrative, and the lack of nighttime danger. 

DL1 didn’t really have an amazing story, mind you, but the narrative here is just terrible. As I got closer to the end, it was a struggle to push on and finish when I just didn’t care about any of the characters or the ending. While I like the touch of adding major decisions to certain parts of the story, even the outcomes just weren’t exciting enough to push the narrative to anything above mid-tier. 
As for the nighttime danger, it’s sad because the game is literally called Dying [i]Light[/i]. In the first game, nighttime often shifted the game from being an action game into a horror game. The tension and change were dramatic and noticeable. I never got the same feeling here. In DL2 night time is more of a stealth or parkour chase in the open world, or rummaging through samey-looking buildings due to the dangerous infected being outside. Even if you are spotted by a Volatile and a chase sequence begins, the AI is so dumb that it simply can’t keep up with the player. As long as you keep moving, there’s really nothing to fear. 

Just like DL1 though, the parkour continues to impress, and I do really like the traversal elements. But damn, if I only cared about the world at all. 
This is a hard one to recommend. As with most 5’s, I often struggle to recommend or not. In the end, I’m going to go with a recommendation. I love DL1, first-person games, RPG mechanics, and zombie games, so my love for the gameplay elements kept me interested enough to finish it, but barely. I would only recommend this if you loved DL1, and even then, prepare to be disappointed. 

[h1] [b] Recommend? (Price) [Y/N] [/b] [/h1]
[h1]Yes[/h1]
$60 is steep. I wouldn’t pay over $15 for this game.

A decent game ruined by corporate greed.

The core game is genuinely good, and there’s a lot to enjoy in Dying Light 2. Unfortunately, Techland’s relentless monetization keeps dragging the experience down. The constant push to buy overpriced cosmetics is bad enough, with loading screens feeling more like advertisements than part of an actual game. And now they want to charge extra for spatial audio in their latest update? Seriously?

At some point, it stops feeling like a company supporting its game and starts feeling like a company squeezing every last penny out of its players. It’s a shame, because the game itself has a solid foundation, but these greedy practices make it difficult to respect the people behind it.

My advice? Stop rewarding this behavior with your money. If you absolutely want to play it, wait for a deep discount. Don’t pay full price just to be bombarded with monetization, and don’t encourage the idea that basic features and overpriced cosmetics are acceptable ways to milk a player base.

Speak with your wallet. The only language these companies seem to understand is money, and if enough players refuse to play along, they might finally reconsider these practices.

You have more power as a consumer than you think. Use it.
